clue.text: Eponymous Southern sucker

parts.note: Terry Southern's comic novel Candy first appeared in Paris under the title of a sweet you suck on a stick, so the sucker gives the book its name

explanation.definitionFit: A boiled sweet on a stick is a sucker, and Terry Southern and Mason Hoffenberg's Candy was first published under that sweet's name.

clue.text: Priestley's Jess finds wooden dory badly damaged

parts.note: oak is a wood, so wooden can be read as made of oak

indicators.note: something badly damaged is knocked out of shape, so the letters of dory are rearranged

explanation.surface: A character in a novel discovers a wrecked old fishing boat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'badly damaged' turns DORY into ROYD, placed after OAK. Jess Oakroyd is the Yorkshire joiner in J. B. Priestley's The Good Companions.
explanation.definitionFit: Jess Oakroyd is the runaway joiner who joins a touring concert party in J. B. Priestley's The Good Companions.

clue.text: Jonathan Oldbuck had this April dish concocted

indicators.note: a dish concocted is made up from its ingredients, so the letters of April dish are mixed into a new order

explanation.surface: A character serves up a seasonal dish of spring food.
explanation.walkthrough: 'concocted' rearranges the nine letters of APRIL DISH. Jonathan Oldbuck is the laird of Monkbarns in Walter Scott's The Antiquary; a laird is a Scottish landowner.
explanation.definitionFit: Oldbuck owns the estate of Monkbarns in Scott's The Antiquary, so he holds the rank and estate of a Scottish landowner.

clue.text: A little——and a pipkin by, / To hold things fitting my necessity" (Herrick, Noble Numbers)

definitions.text: A little——and a pipkin by, / To hold things fitting my necessity" (Herrick, Noble Numbers)

parts.words: A little——and a pipkin by, / To hold things fitting my necessity" (Herrick, Noble Numbers)
parts.note: a gap in Herrick's poem A Thanksgiving to God for his House, to be filled with a small wooden pail set beside a little earthen pot

explanation.definitionFit: The missing word is a small wooden vessel, a pail or ladle, which Herrick names alongside a pipkin, a small clay pot.

clue.text: Sharpe's rare steak?

parts.note: Tom Sharpe wrote a comic Cambridge novel whose title reads as a thick cut of beef cooked as underdone as possible, blue being the rarest grade

explanation.definitionFit: A porterhouse is a thick beef cut and a steak served blue is barely seared; the phrase is also the title of Tom Sharpe's college satire.

clue.text: Fitzgerald's night, and as 5 should be

explanation.definitionFit: F. Scott Fitzgerald's novel is Tender Is the Night, and a good steak (the answer to 5) should be soft and easy to cut.

clue.text: Artist spotting new canvas

parts.note: a painter of the 1950s French school that built pictures from dabs and blots of colour, so spotting means applying spots rather than noticing

explanation.definitionFit: Tachisme, from French tache 'stain, spot', was a post-war abstract style of splashed dabs; its painters dotted their canvases with colour.

clue.text: He wrote two thirds of 26

parts.note: 26 is a group of six; two thirds of six is four, and this novelist wrote a famous four-novel sequence set in Alexandria

explanation.walkthrough: 26 is SESTET, six; two thirds of it is four, a quartet, and Lawrence Durrell wrote The Alexandria Quartet.
explanation.definitionFit: Lawrence Durrell wrote The Alexandria Quartet, four linked novels, which is two thirds of a group of six.

clue.text: What on earth was Neruda writing about?

definitions.text: What on earth was Neruda writing about?

parts.words: What on earth was Neruda writing about?
parts.note: Pablo Neruda's poetry collection Residencia en la tierra names a dwelling on earth, so the question's 'on earth' is part of the title rather than an exclamation

explanation.definitionFit: Neruda's collection Residencia en la tierra translates as a dwelling place on earth, so a home is what he wrote of.

clue.text: "Five years ago, she told me, they met Dieter on a — holiday in Germany " (Le Carr, Call for the Dead)

definitions.text: "Five years ago, she told me, they met Dieter on a — holiday in Germany " (Le Carr, Call for the Dead)

parts.words: "Five years ago, she told me, they met Dieter on a — holiday in Germany " (Le Carr, Call for the Dead)
parts.note: a gap in a line from John le Carré's first Smiley novel, to be filled with the kind of winter holiday spent on snowy slopes

explanation.definitionFit: The missing word describes a holiday spent sliding down snowy mountains on long runners, completing le Carré's sentence.

clue.text: Whose things did Raphael portray?

parts.note: not the Renaissance painter but Frederic Raphael, whose 1973 novel is named for the belongings of a dead man called Richard

explanation.walkthrough: Raphael the painter is the false path; Frederic Raphael wrote the novel Richard's Things.
explanation.definitionFit: Frederic Raphael's novel Richard's Things takes its title from the possessions of the dead husband Richard.

clue.text: Source of wealth offered by Smith. Or just a claim to possession?

definitions.text: Source of wealth offered by Smith

parts.note: or is the heraldic word for the colour gold
saying 'mine' claims something as your own

explanation.surface: A novelist offers riches, or perhaps just stakes a claim to them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Or' looks like a conjunction but is heraldic gold. Wilbur Smith wrote the novel Gold Mine.
explanation.definitionFit: A mine yielding precious metal is a figurative byword for any rich source of money, and Wilbur Smith's novel bears that title.

clue.text: Definitely in the title

parts.note: a deed is the legal document proving title to property

explanation.surface: Someone is sure to be named in the heading.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words are emphatic adverbs of assent: 'yes, certainly'.

clue.text: Van Sant's was his own and private

definitions.text: Van Sant's was his own and private

parts.words: Van Sant's was his own and private
parts.note: Gus Van Sant directed the film My Own Private ... named after a western American state

explanation.definitionFit: Gus Van Sant's 1991 film is My Own Private Idaho, so the state is the one he called his own and private.

clue.text: Announces to close friends, in a hint I'm a test-setter in Eng. Lit.

indicators.note: in tells us the answer sits inside the run of words that follows it

explanation.surface: An examiner of English literature drops a hint to their friends.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run across 'hINT I'M A TESt-setter'. It also means 'announces' as a verb and 'close friends' as a plural noun.
explanation.definitionFit: To hint or make known is to announce, and people with whom you are very close are your confidants.

clue.text: French moggie sick on French poet Walter from here

parts.note: chat is French for cat; moggie is British slang for a cat
ill means sick

explanation.surface: A French cat has been ill on a French poet.
explanation.walkthrough: Walter of Châtillon was a twelfth-century poet who wrote in Latin; the town is his birthplace.
explanation.definitionFit: The medieval poet Walter took his name from the French town of his birth, so the town is where he came from.

clue.text: Recklessly rob titles for opera books

indicators.note: done recklessly, the letters of rob titles are thrown about into a new order

explanation.surface: A thief carelessly steals titles intended for opera texts.
explanation.definitionFit: The printed words of an opera are its texts, sold as small booklets to the audience.

clue.text: Towers arose in Barsetshire from this family

definitions.text: Towers arose in Barsetshire from this family

parts.words: Towers arose in Barsetshire from this family
parts.note: Trollope's Barchester Towers is set in his invented county of Barsetshire, and the clue names a family connected with the towers

explanation.definitionFit: The surname belongs to a family linked with Trollope's Barsetshire, the county of Barchester Towers.

clue.text: Camus theme follows closely, according to Adams

definitions.text: Camus theme follows closely, according to Adams

parts.words: Camus theme follows closely, according to Adams
parts.note: Camus wrote La Peste; add a word for 'follows closely', dogs, and you have Richard Adams's novel about two escaped laboratory animals

explanation.walkthrough: 'follows closely' is DOGS: Richard Adams wrote The Plague Dogs, so the Camus theme is followed by dogs.
explanation.definitionFit: Camus's La Peste is known in English as the name of a deadly epidemic disease, the first part of Richard Adams's title.

clue.text: Makes certain, starting English Novel studies under regular enquiry system

indicators.note: starting points to the opening letter of each of the seven words that follow

parts.words: English Novel studies under regular enquiry system

explanation.surface: An English literature course is kept on track by a system of regular questioning.
explanation.definitionFit: To guarantee is to make sure of an outcome, the same verb sense.

clue.text: One of those stripped and whipped by Wither, possibly

definitions.text: One of those stripped and whipped by Wither, possibly

parts.words: One of those stripped and whipped by Wither, possibly
parts.note: George Wither's satire ... Stript and Whipt (1613) flayed vices, so one of them is a single wrong of that kind

explanation.definitionFit: George Wither's satire Abuses Stript and Whipt attacked misuses and wrongs, so one target is a single misuse.

clue.text: Symphonic composer with Bohemian lifestyle-

parts.note: a writer of symphonic poems who came from Bohemia, so 'Bohemian' is his homeland rather than an arty way of life

explanation.definitionFit: Bedřich Smetana, a Czech from Bohemia, wrote the cycle of symphonic poems Má vlast.

clue.text: Fear of Machen

parts.note: Arthur Machen's 1917 novella about animals turning on mankind is titled with a word for extreme fear

explanation.definitionFit: Arthur Machen's novella The Terror is named for intense fear, which its rural wartime killings spread.

clue.text: Way shown by Evelyn Underhill

parts.note: Evelyn Underhill, a writer on spirituality

explanation.definitionFit: Underhill's book The Mystic Way traces the spiritual path of those seeking direct union with God.

clue.text: Former example sees false interpretations

parts.note: ex means former, as in an ex-partner
e.g. is the abbreviation for 'for example'

indicators.note: false means not genuine, so the letters of sees are rearranged into a counterfeit order

explanation.surface: A former instance sees mistaken readings of a text.
explanation.walkthrough: 'false' turns SEES into ESES, placed after EX and EG.
explanation.definitionFit: Explanations of a text, especially scripture, are its critical readings or commentaries.

clue.text: Change direction of decree for Eliot's doctor

parts.note: to turn is to change direction
a bull is a formal papal decree

explanation.surface: A novelist's physician makes a legal ruling go the other way.
explanation.walkthrough: A bull here is a papal edict. Dr Turnbull is a medical man in George Eliot's Middlemarch.
explanation.definitionFit: George Eliot gives the name to a medical practitioner in Middlemarch.

clue.text: Mo Hayder's ceremony

parts.note: Mo Hayder's 2008 crime novel takes its title from a word for a set ceremonial observance

explanation.definitionFit: Mo Hayder's thriller is called Ritual, a word for a formal religious rite or ceremony.

clue.text: Two trilogies might make one

parts.note: two sets of three make a set of six, and a group of six lines closes a sonnet

explanation.definitionFit: A group of six, such as the last six lines of a Petrarchan sonnet, is made of two threes.

clue.text: Places visited by Lawrence

parts.note: D. H. Lawrence's travel book ... Places describes the tombs of ancient Italy, so the clue names the people of that region

explanation.definitionFit: D. H. Lawrence's travel book Etruscan Places records his visits to the tombs of ancient Etruria in Italy.
